title: The Body, Health & a Pharmacy Visit Overview
subtitle: Listen to the lesson explained in English

transcript.en: Welcome! 👋 Unit 13: The Body, Health and a Pharmacy Visit.
Nobody plans to get ill on holiday, or in a new country, but it happens. Today you learn the body, how to say what hurts, and how to get through a visit to the pharmacy. Let's go!
🦶 PART 1: THE BODY 🦶
Start at the top. The head:
the eye:
the back:
and the belly:
Then the hand:
and the foot:
For now, learn each word on its own. Later in the unit you will see what happens when there are two of them. 💡
🤒 PART 2: FEELING ROUGH 🤒
Almost every complaint in Maltese is built the same way: I have, then whatever is wrong. The pain:
so I have a headache is, literally, I have pain of the head:
The fever:
and a cold:
A cold takes no article. And it is not the word for cold weather, which is a different word altogether. 💡
Now the tonsils:
A sore throat in Maltese is pain in the tonsils. You will hear it in the conversation in a moment. 💡
And the two words you need at the counter. The pharmacy:
and the prescription:
💊 PART 3: AT THE PHARMACY 💊
Mary walks into the village pharmacy. The pharmacist asks how he can help:
Mary is not feeling well today:

transcript.mt: Bonġu. Mhux qed inħossni sew illum.

transcript.en: She has a headache and a temperature:

transcript.mt: Għandi uġigħ ta' ras u għandi d-deni.

transcript.en: and since yesterday, a sore throat too:
He tells her to take the medicine twice a day, and rest:

transcript.mt: Ħu din il-mediċina darbtejn kuljum, u strieħ.

transcript.en: And the good news, she does not need a prescription:
👆 PART 4: ONES, TWOS AND MANYS 👆
Here is something most learners never meet. Maltese counts in three steps, not two: one, many, and a special form for exactly two. The hand:
and a pair of hands:
The foot:
and a pair of feet:
Listen for the ending. The pair form usually finishes in an e-n sound or an a-n sound, and things that come in twos almost always use it. 💡
Time takes it too. One week:
and two weeks:
Not every word has a pair form. For two days, Maltese switches to a different word for day. I have been ill for two days:
📖 PART 5: SAYING NO IN THE PRESENT 📖
You already know how to say no in the past: one piece in front of the verb and one on the end. The present works exactly the same way. I don't understand:
and I don't eat meat:
Before a vowel, or before the letters g-h and h, the front piece shrinks to just an m with an apostrophe. I don't have a temperature:
and there's no pharmacy here:
🎉 THAT'S UNIT 13 🎉
The body, what hurts, and a whole visit to the pharmacy. Tap a card to flip it, use Play all to hear a whole section hands-free, and try the exercises. Well done, and stay healthy!
